newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah strengthens on tight liquidity.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah strengthens on tight liquidity.

text.p: Indonesia's rupiah strengthened against the dollar in late trading on Monday on the back of tight liquidity, dealers said.
One U.S. bank dealer said liquidity remained the issue due to the approaching lunar new year on February 7 and the Eid al-Fitr celebration on February 9 and 10.
"Trading is mainly liquidity-driven. I think the condition might only stabilise next week," one local bank dealer said.
He said the market might even turn ample when all the money being withdrawn at present returns to the system.
Interbank rates were edging up, driven by rises in the swap market, some dealers said. Overnight money was at 18.0 percent. Overnight swaps were at 1.0/1.1 and tom/next at 1.1/1.2 points.
The U.S. bank dealer said offshore operators were squeezed if they continued to go long in dollars because of the expensive short-term swap premiums.
"I think they would be forced to unload soon," one said.
Spot rupiah was at 2,373.75/74.50 at 0900 GMT, compared with an opening of 2,375.8/76.5. Tomorrow and today rupiah closed at 2,372.5/73.0 and 2,373.0/73.5, respectively.
One-month swaps were at 15.20/15.50, two at 29.0/30.5, three at 40.0/42.0 and six at 80.0/80.5 points.
The central bank kept its intervention band at 2,372/2,564 and the conversion band at 2,372/2,420 on Monday.
The bank depreciated the rupiah by three points last week after lowering it by two points the previous week.
